title: Depth of a binary quadratic formal hypersurface
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $S=F[[u,v]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $\mathfrak p=(u,v)$ and $Q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ for $a,b,c\in F$ not all zero. Then $S$ has depth $2$ and the local ring $S/(Q)$, whose maximal ideal is $\mathfrak p/(Q)$, has depth $1$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]. These conclusions hold in every characteristic; in particular they hold whenever $b^2-4ac\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), proof of (1) implies (3), explicit depth computation for the quadratic model; Tag 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), equivalence (2) and (3). The regular-sequence/depth-drop argument is detailed in the repair report.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] with coefficient field $F$ and $d=2$. Thus $S$ is a nonzero Noetherian local integral domain, its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak p=(u,v)$, and it is regular of dimension $2$. Apply [lem-trf-regular-local-regular-sequence-depth] to $S$ and the empty sequence ($c=i=0$). This gives $\operatorname{depth}(S)=\dim S=2$.

source.place: Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary), field case; Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM), final assertion.

proof.text: By the coefficientwise definition of formal power series, the coefficients of $Q$ at the distinct exponent pairs $(2,0),(1,1),(0,2)$ are respectively $a,b,c$. At least one is nonzero, so $Q\ne0$. Also $Q=u(au+bv)+v(cv)$ lies in $\mathfrak p$. Since $S$ is an integral domain by step 1, $Qz=0$ forces $z=0$: multiplication by $Q$ on $S$ is injective. In particular $I=(Q)\subseteq\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Coefficient expansion of the quadratic model in Curves Tag 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), proof of (1) implies (3); elementary coefficient calculation.

proof.text: Regard $M=S$ as an $S$-module, generated by $1$ and nonzero by step 1. The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-depth-drops-by-one] hold: $S$ is Noetherian local, and step 2 gives $Q\in\mathfrak p$ and injective multiplication by $Q$. Therefore $S/QS\ne0$ and $\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak p}(S/QS)=\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak p}(S)-1=2-1=1$.

Put $B=S/(Q)=S/QS$. It is a finite $S$-module generated by the class of $1$, and $IB=0$ because every multiple of $Q$ is zero in this quotient. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-depth-over-quotient-ring] with $R=S$, $I=(Q)$ and $M=B$; step 2 verifies $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Its statement gives the Noetherian local ring $B$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak p/(Q)$, and identifies its ring depth with the $S$-module depth in step 3. Thus $\operatorname{depth}(B)=1$. No step restricts the characteristic or uses the discriminant, so this applies in every characteristic, including the stated nonzero-discriminant case.
